patients.name: Patient_001_Urgent_Potassium
patients.demo_beat: The agent identified three independent potassium-raising drugs coexisting in this patient's regimen. None alone would push K+ to 6.1; the combination explains the magnitude.
active_conditions_summary: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
patients.notes: Headline demo case (CLAUDE.md §10 Patient 1). Trend RISING: 4.6 → 4.8 → 5.4 → 6.1 over 12 months. Three K+-raising drug classes coexist.

patients.name: Patient_002_Creatinine_Trend
patients.demo_beat: Single result interpreted in context: this isn't 'mild renal impairment' — it's an acute change in a patient where two drugs (an ARB and an NSAID) compromise renal perfusion synergistically.
patients.notes: CLAUDE.md §10 Patient 2. Creatinine 2.1 with prior 1.4 → large delta (0.7) AND rising. Naproxen + Losartan combination.

patients.name: Patient_003_A1c_Chronic
patients.demo_beat: The agent correctly distinguishes between an emergency (potassium 6.1) and a scheduled follow-up (poorly controlled A1c). Even at 9.8%, HbA1c never escalates to URGENT in this demo — it's chronic.
patients.notes: CLAUDE.md §10 Patient 3. A1c 9.8% with established T2DM. No A1c-raising medications. SOON, not URGENT.

patient_4_strategy: Patient 4 (INSUFFICIENT_DATA case) is intentionally left to be created as a fresh empty patient inside Prompt Opinion's UI rather than as a Bundle. A patient with no medications, no conditions, no prior labs, and a borderline K+ of 5.3 will trigger our INSUFFICIENT_DATA fail-safe in classify_lab_followup_urgency.
